name: TRIPOD (2015)
source: Collins GS, Reitsma JB, Altman DG, Moons KGM. Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis Or Diagnosis (TRIPOD): the TRIPOD Statement. Ann Intern Med. 2015;162(1):55-63 / BMC Med. 2015;13:1. https://www.tripod-statement.org/resources/ | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4284921/

items.text: Identify the study as developing or validating a multivariable prediction model, naming target population and outcome.
Summarize objectives, design, setting, participants, sample size, predictors, outcome, statistical methods, results, and conclusions.
Explain the diagnostic or prognostic clinical context and rationale, referencing existing prediction models.
Specify study objectives, stating whether the report covers model development, validation, or both.
Describe study design or data sources separately for development and validation datasets.
Specify key study dates, including accrual start, accrual end, and end of follow-up.
Describe the study setting, including number and geographic location of participating centers.
Specify participant eligibility criteria.
Describe treatments received by participants, if relevant to predictions.
Clearly define the predicted outcome, including how and when it was assessed.
Report any measures taken to blind assessment of the predicted outcome.
Clearly define all predictors used in model development or validation, including measurement methods and timing.
Report any measures taken to blind assessment of predictors for outcome and other predictors.
Explain how the study sample size was determined.
Describe how missing data were handled, including details of any imputation procedures.
Explain how candidate predictors were coded or transformed in statistical analyses.
Specify model type, model-building and predictor-selection procedures, and internal validation methods.
For validation, describe how individual risk predictions were calculated from the model.
Specify all metrics used to evaluate model performance and compare competing models.
Describe any model updating, such as recalibration, performed during validation.
Explain how risk groups were defined and created, if used.
Identify any differences between development and validation datasets in setting, eligibility, outcome, or predictors.
Describe participant flow, including counts with and without the outcome and follow-up duration.
Summarize participant demographics, clinical features, predictor distributions, and missing-data counts.
For validation, compare distributions of key demographics, predictors, and outcomes against development data.
Report the number of participants and outcome events included in each analysis.
Report unadjusted associations between each candidate predictor and the outcome, if evaluated.
Present the full prediction model, including all regression coefficients and intercept or baseline survival.
Explain how clinicians or users apply the prediction model to individual patients.
Report model performance measures together with confidence intervals.
Report updated model specifications and performance metrics if model updating was performed.
Discuss study limitations, such as sample representativeness, low events per predictor, or missing data.
Interpret validation findings relative to model performance in development and other validation datasets.
Give an overall interpretation considering objectives, limitations, similar studies, and other relevant evidence.
Discuss potential clinical utility of the prediction model and directions for future research.
State availability of supplementary materials such as protocol, web calculator, or datasets.
Report funding sources and the role of funders in the study.
